P.title: Pipeline width (sustained NOPs per cycle)

P.title: Register moves per cycle (mov x, x)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent register moves over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 10.00.

P.title: Integer adds that all read one register
P.note: Highest sustained rate of add xN, x19, x19 (every instance reads the same register twice) over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.01. Not close to an integer: the unit count is probably the next integer up, not reached because of scheduler balancing.

P.title: Reorder buffer capacity in NOPs
P.note: NOPs need no register and no scheduler entry, only room in the reorder buffer. Apple cores pack several such instructions into one reorder-buffer entry, so this is far more than the number of ordinary instructions that fit. Overlap is lost between 3358 and 3368 fillers (time ratio 1.02 -> 1.53); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Integer register renames in flight
P.note: Each filler writes an integer register, so each holds a fresh physical register until it retires. Add the 31 architectural registers for the file's total size. Overlap is lost between 394 and 395 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.78); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: 32-bit integer register renames in flight
P.note: Fillers write w registers. If this is about twice the 64-bit figure, two 32-bit values share one physical register. Overlap is lost between 806 and 809 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.68); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: FP/SIMD register renames in flight

P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Flag renames in flight
P.note: Each filler (cmp) writes only NZCV. Overlap is lost between 167 and 168 fillers (time ratio 1.02 -> 1.87).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Unresolved-branch capacity
P.note: Fillers are never-taken cbz instructions. Overlap is lost between 194 and 195 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.82).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Store queue
P.note: Fillers are stores, which hold a store-queue entry until after retirement. Overlap is lost between 137 and 138 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.81).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Load queue
P.note: Fillers are FP loads that hit the L1 cache; they finish at once but hold their load-queue entry until retirement. Overlap is lost between 483 and 485 fillers (time ratio 1.02 -> 1.58); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.

P.title: Reorder buffer capacity in ordinary instructions

P.title: aese + aesmc as one operation

P.title: Branch misprediction penalty
P.note: One iteration takes 1.50 cycles when the branch alternates and 9.87 when it follows random bits; twice the difference is the cost of one misprediction, assuming half of the random branches are mispredicted (that rate cannot be read without PMU events, hence the confidence). The branch's condition is ready before it is renamed, so this is the shortest penalty the pipeline has.

P.title: L1 load-to-use latency (pointer chase)
P.note: ldr x1, [x1] over a buffer of 16 to 32 KiB. Register-offset addressing adds a cycle (see the instruction table).

P.title: L1 data cache capacity
P.note: Largest buffer that still loads in 3.0 cycles; the next size tried (135 KiB) is slower. The OS reports 128 KiB.

P.title: L2 load-to-use latency, small footprint
P.note: Pointer chase over 256 to 512 KiB: past the L1 cache and still covered by the first-level TLB.

P.title: L2 load-to-use latency, large footprint
P.note: Pointer chase over 2048 to 8192 KiB. Includes first-level TLB misses where the footprint exceeds the TLB's reach.

P.title: L2 cache capacity seen by one core
P.note: Latency passes twice the large-footprint L2 latency between 16384 and 23170 KiB. The OS reports 16384 KiB shared by 4 cores; the other cores were busy, so one core sees less than the whole cache.

P.title: Load latency from memory (128 MiB random chase)
P.note: 348 cycles at the clock observed; includes TLB misses (16 KiB pages). Depends on the memory fitted and on what else uses it.

P.title: First-level data TLB entries
P.note: One cell per 16 KiB page against the same cells packed together: translation is free up to 162 pages and costs more from 166 on.
P.ylabel: extra cycles per load (one cell per page)

P.title: Second-level TLB entries
P.note: A first-level TLB miss that the second level catches costs about 6.0 cycles. From 3170 pages on (3101 were still fine) the cost passes 12.0 cycles: page walks. See the first-level entry for the curve.

P.title: Latency of a load that always returns the same value
P.note: ldr x0, [x0] chasing a cell that points to itself takes 0.34 cycles per load; the same load walking a ring of 509 cells takes 3.03. The constant value is predicted, so the chain no longer waits for the load: a self-pointing cell cannot be used to measure load latency here. The curve shows how many alternating values are still predicted.
P.xlabel: distinct values each load returns in turn

P.title: add + csel chained through the input csel does not select
P.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; csel x0, x21, x1, ne with the flags never written, so x21 is always chosen. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (0.33 to 2.00, mean 1.05). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: The same chain after 64 iterations of the opposite outcome
P.note: Identical code at new addresses, with 64 iterations of the opposite condition between training and measurement. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (2.00 to 2.00, mean 2.00). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: The same chain with csinc (control)
P.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; csinc x0, x21, x1, ne. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (2.00 to 2.00, mean 2.00). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of csel when its condition has never changed
P.note: Chain of add x1, x0, #1 and csel x0, x1, x21, ne with the flags never written. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 0.85 to 1.00 (mean 0.92). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of the same csel after 64 iterations of the other outcome
P.note: Identical code at new addresses; after the same training it runs 64 iterations with the opposite condition, then is measured with the usual one. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 1.00 to 1.00 (mean 1.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of csinc under the same conditions (control)
P.note: csinc cannot be replaced by a move. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 1.00 to 1.00 (mean 1.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of mov x0, x1 in the same loops (reference)
P.note: What a fully eliminated move looks like in this loop. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 0.00 to 0.00 (mean 0.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Two serialised cache misses when the data are pointers
P.note: Two independent chases, each missing the cache, with 1000 adds between them so that the second cannot enter the window until the first retires. Relative to a loop with one chase this costs 1.67x when the cells hold indices and 1.36x when they hold pointers. The pointers are being dereferenced ahead of the program: a data-memory-dependent prefetcher is at work, and it hides the second miss.

E.note: Latency of one AES round through the state: 2.56 cycles for aese immediately followed by aesmc, 5.12 with a NOP between them (aese alone 2.50, aesmc alone 2.50). The adjacent pair runs as a single operation.

E.title: Branch misprediction penalty
E.note: One iteration takes 3.00 cycles when the branch alternates and 8.88 when it follows random bits; twice the difference is the cost of one misprediction, assuming half of the random branches are mispredicted (that rate cannot be read without PMU events, hence the confidence). The branch's condition is ready before it is renamed, so this is the shortest penalty the pipeline has.

E.title: L1 load-to-use latency (pointer chase)
E.note: ldr x1, [x1] over a buffer of 16 to 32 KiB. Register-offset addressing adds a cycle (see the instruction table).

E.title: L1 data cache capacity
E.note: Largest buffer that still loads in 3.0 cycles; the next size tried (67 KiB) is slower. The OS reports 64 KiB.

E.title: L2 load-to-use latency, small footprint
E.note: Pointer chase over 128 to 256 KiB: past the L1 cache and still covered by the first-level TLB.

E.title: L2 load-to-use latency, large footprint
E.note: Pointer chase over 1024 to 4096 KiB. Includes first-level TLB misses where the footprint exceeds the TLB's reach.

E.title: L2 cache capacity seen by one core
E.note: Latency passes twice the large-footprint L2 latency between 5793 and 8192 KiB. The OS reports 6144 KiB shared by 6 cores; the other cores were busy, so one core sees less than the whole cache.

E.title: Load latency from memory (128 MiB random chase)
E.note: 254 cycles at the clock observed; includes TLB misses (16 KiB pages). Depends on the memory fitted and on what else uses it.

E.title: First-level data TLB entries
E.note: One cell per 16 KiB page against the same cells packed together: translation is free up to 133 pages and costs more from 136 on.
E.ylabel: extra cycles per load (one cell per page)

E.title: Second-level TLB entries
E.note: A first-level TLB miss that the second level catches costs about 10.3 cycles. From 2435 pages on (2386 were still fine) the cost passes 20.6 cycles: page walks. See the first-level entry for the curve.

E.title: Latency of a load that always returns the same value
E.note: ldr x0, [x0] chasing a cell that points to itself takes 3.00 cycles per load; the same load walking a ring of 509 cells takes 2.99. No value prediction is visible: both agree.
E.xlabel: distinct values each load returns in turn

E.title: add + csel chained through the input csel does not select
E.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; csel x0, x21, x1, ne with the flags never written, so x21 is always chosen. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (2.00 to 2.00, mean 2.00). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: The same chain after 64 iterations of the opposite outcome
E.note: Identical code at new addresses, with 64 iterations of the opposite condition between training and measurement. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (2.00 to 2.00, mean 2.00). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: The same chain with csinc (control)
E.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; csinc x0, x21, x1, ne. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (2.00 to 2.00, mean 2.00). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: Latency of csel when its condition has never changed
E.note: Chain of add x1, x0, #1 and csel x0, x1, x21, ne with the flags never written. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 1.00 to 1.00 (mean 1.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: Latency of the same csel after 64 iterations of the other outcome
E.note: Identical code at new addresses; after the same training it runs 64 iterations with the opposite condition, then is measured with the usual one. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 1.00 to 1.00 (mean 1.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: Latency of csinc under the same conditions (control)
E.note: csinc cannot be replaced by a move. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 1.00 to 1.00 (mean 1.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: Latency of mov x0, x1 in the same loops (reference)
E.note: What a fully eliminated move looks like in this loop. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 0.01 to 0.38 (mean 0.30). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
E.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

E.title: Two serialised cache misses when the data are pointers
E.note: Two independent chases, each missing the cache, with 1000 adds between them so that the second cannot enter the window until the first retires. Relative to a loop with one chase this costs 1.60x when the cells hold indices and 1.53x when they hold pointers. No difference: nothing prefetches through the pointers here.
